questions.q: What is the purpose of the hydrogel modification in aqueous rechargeable zinc iodine batteries?

questions.q: What effect does the hydrogel modification have on the shuttle effect in zinc iodine batteries?
questions.answer: It mitigates the diffusion back and forth of polysulfide between anode and cathode, the so-called 'shuttle effect'.

questions.q: What effect does the hydrogel electrolyte have on the iodine conversion reaction on the cathode side?
questions.answer: It accelerates the iodine conversion reaction on the cathode side.

triples.o: iodine conversion reaction on cathode side

questions.q: What functional groups do the anode and cathode of the hydrogel have?

questions.q: What is the effect of the hydrogel on the anode side of the battery?
questions.answer: It repels dissolved polyiodides, allowing zinc to be deposited uniformly and protecting the anode from iodine-caused corrosion.

questions.q: What is the effect of the hydrogel on the cathode side of the battery?
questions.answer: Polyiodides are immobilized, and redox reactions are sped up thanks to synchronized rapid transport of ions and electrons.

questions.q: What is the effect of the solid nature of the hydrogel electrolyte on dendrite growth?
questions.answer: It can limit the growth of dendrites thanks to its mechanical strength, which acts as a physical barrier not present in liquid electrolytes.
